rv.q: Whatever world Xhloe and Natasha are building, we need to see more of it.
Then the Rodeo Burned Down, Xhloe and Natasha have created a work of rare imagination and startling originality.
An absolute joy, a jostling ride, an evening of constant surprise, all of that describes what it’s like to watch clown pair Xhloe and Natasha tell the story of their love for the rodeo.
The show balances a scrappiness with inventiveness and a dinginess with something magical.
With its meta-theatrical plot twist, Rodeo proves that Xhloe and Natasha know exactly what they’re doing.
On second viewing, the production seems even better.
Nevertheless, And Then the Rodeo Burned Down , is one fascinating maverick of an entertainment.
It may simply be a good example of a piece developed for a local audience that doesn't travel well.
A two-clown wrecking crew turns rodeo labor and theatrical precarity into the funniest indictment of the industry you'll see this season.
This rodeo is absurd and on fire … literally

cn.t: Critics largely embrace this absurdist clown show for its inventive physical comedy and warmhearted oddity, though some find the experimental humor doesn't land. The duo's acrobatic performances and surreal take on Americana win widespread praise.

vr.q: And the Rodeo burned down is definitely going to be a Broadway Ben must see.
The way the two of them navigate the movement and the emotional beats in perfect synchronicity is marvelous and worth the price of admission in itself
even with my reservations I still appreciated that the show left a lot to chew on as their work tends to do making me laugh and feel and think pretty consistently throughout
